title: Thursday: the biggest T-bane shutdown starts today
intro: 63 of 101 metro stations close until Sunday night. Plan extra time if you must travel.

big-news.text: Oslo's largest-ever T-bane shutdown is underway until Sunday night: 63 of 101 stations are closed, nothing runs through the city centre, and lines 4 and 5 are fully shut. Only short western stretches of lines 1, 2 and 3 still operate.
Equinor is still fighting a cyberattack that began Tuesday evening. Production is unaffected so far, and the company says there are no signs that data was stolen.

whats-changing.text: Southern Norway may face one of its priciest power winters in years — spot prices near 2 kr/kWh before grid fees. Households on Norgespris are largely shielded; others still rely on strømstøtte.

oslo.text: Replacement buses 2B, 3B and 25B run to Majorstuen; tram 19x continues into the centre. Ruter urges you not to travel unless you must — buses were already crowded by 08:00.
oslo.takeaway: Working from home or walking/cycling beats sitting in a packed bus this week.

oslo.text: Oslo Taxi reports far more bookings than a normal Thursday. Pre-booking slots for Thursday and Friday mornings were already full early today.

be-aware.text: PST says a terror attempt in Norway in the coming year is likely; the national threat level stays at 3 of 5 (elevated).
Statens vegvesen expects heavier car traffic and queues. If you must drive, avoid rush hours.

fun-and-free.text: Jul i Vinterland continues at Spikersuppa — ice rink, Christmas market stalls and lights in the centre (paid skating; browsing is free).
